svg.title: The epistemic backlog
svg.desc: Four complete graphs of 4, 8, 16 and 32 artifacts, drawn at the same size, hold 6, 28, 120 and 496 possible pairs; one pair in the largest is marked as the one that matters. A key below shows the four kinds of content in the epistemic backlog.
svg.text: Among n artifacts there are n(n − 1)/2 possible pairs. Each time the record doubles, the possible pairs roughly quadruple, while the people reading and their
The green pair is the one that matters.
In the record it carries no mark.
These conditions create an epistemic backlog: a collection of recoverable observations, potentially meaningful relationships, unresolved contradictions, and
Something recorded that can be got back.
A place where two records disagree and
no one has worked out why.

Pair counts are arithmetic, n(n − 1)/2, not counts from any corpus. Every graph is drawn at the same size, so density stands for the growth: partners per artifact grow in step with
n, pairs with its square. Nothing in the record marks which pairs matter.
